manual_findings.title: Returning from a grid replay leaves a contradictory success message on screen
manual_findings.affected_ui: Current-input result summary and workbench status paragraph below it
reproduction: Open the default Crossing cart example.
Choose the cell named '1.20 metres per second, 3.0 seconds delay: Goal reached. Replay'.
Read the result summary and status paragraph; playing the restored simulation and opening Scene files do not clear the stale message.

observed.grid_selected_result: Goal reached · Grid replay: 1.20 m/s · +3.0 s cart delay; Travel time 9.28 s; Closest gap 0.23 m
observed.restored_result: Contact with Crossing cart · Current inputs · deterministic simulation; Travel time 4.13 s; Closest gap 0.00 m
observed.status_still_visible: Replaying 1.20 m/s with 3.0 s extra delay: Goal reached.
observed.verification: Exact text confirmed in the accessibility tree, read-only DOM inspection, and a screenshot showing both contradictory statements.

manual_findings.impact: Users returning to their own scene can mistake a successful test case for the current experiment's outcome. Assistive technology also receives no updated status explaining the return.
manual_findings.recommendation: Update or clear the workbench status when returning to current settings; explicitly confirm that the current experiment is active.

manual_findings.title: Configuration tabs do not respond to the expected arrow-key navigation

observed.click_results: Clicking Robot and Route successfully revealed their respective configuration panels.

manual_findings.impact: Keyboard and screen-reader users encountering a tablist cannot move between tabs using its expected left/right interaction. The controls remain available as ordinary Tab stops, so this is not a complete task blocker.
manual_findings.recommendation: Support directional navigation between tabs with a single tab stop, selected-state updates, and consistent panel activation.
manual_findings.limitation: This is a directly observed interaction-pattern defect, not a claim of an independently certified accessibility-standard violation.

manual_checks.name: Keyboard route editing and undo
manual_checks.evidence: ArrowRight on Move Start changed Start from (1.2, 4.0) to (1.3, 4.0), changed the selected handle, enabled Undo, and recalculated travel time from 4.13 s to 4.04 s. Undo restored (1.2, 4.0), the 4.13 s result, and announced 'Change undone.'.

manual_checks.name: Stress-test generation
manual_checks.evidence: Default case produced 45 trial controls: 5 speeds × 9 delays. The UI reported 23 of 45 sampled cases did not reach the goal and explicitly said this is not a probability or safety score.

manual_checks.name: Grid result accessibility
manual_checks.evidence: The table has a descriptive caption, 10 column headers with scope=col, 5 speed row headers with scope=row, and 45 named buttons. Each button's accessible name includes speed, delay, outcome, and replay action; icons also distinguish goal/contact/time-limit outcomes.

manual_checks.name: Grid replay and return
manual_checks.result: replay and numeric results worked; status defect B-01
manual_checks.evidence: The 1.20 m/s +3.0 s cell selected successfully, focused the replay heading, and displayed Goal reached / 9.28 s / 0.23 m. Return to my settings restored Contact with Crossing cart / 4.13 s / 0.00 m.

manual_checks.name: 3D rendering and simulation playback
manual_checks.evidence: 3D view replaced the editable plan with a rendered scene. Play simulation changed to Pause simulation and advanced replay from 0 to 0.24 s; it later returned to Play simulation at 4.13/4.13 s. Console remained empty.

manual_checks.name: Accessible names and landmarks
manual_checks.evidence: The page exposes header, named Main navigation, main, footer, a skip-to-editor link, named plan handles, labeled visible fields, and polite live result/status regions. No button lacked all of text, aria-label, aria-labelledby, and title in the inspected DOM.

manual_checks.name: File-entry UI
manual_checks.evidence: The expanded section presents named Choose 2D floorplan, Choose 3D model, and Load experiment JSON controls. Supported types and local-processing limits are described. Hidden file inputs use display:none and are activated through named visible controls.
manual_checks.limitation: No imports, uploads, malformed-file tests, or exports were performed.

manual_checks.name: Default viewport layout
manual_checks.evidence: At 1280×720 CSS px, document scrollWidth equaled viewport width (1280); no document-wide horizontal overflow was present in the initial state. The same viewport dimensions were recorded before close.
manual_checks.limitation: No responsive, zoom, reduced-motion, or full contrast audit was performed.

evidence: Both observed GitHub links opening new tabs use rel=noreferrer.
The inspected DOM contained no absolute http(s) external script, iframe, image, or stylesheet URLs.
The file-entry UI states local processing and explicitly calls imported geometry an approximation.
No unexpected dialog, permission prompt, or secret exposure was observed in the sampled flows.
security_observations.limitation: UI/DOM observations only. No complete network capture, backend/header audit, uploaded-model validation, malicious-input testing, or proof of local-only processing was attempted.

false_positive_notes: There were no CLI detector findings to adjudicate.
Unlabeled hidden file inputs were not reported as a UI accessibility defect: they were display:none and paired with named visible trigger buttons.
The screenshot's apparent simultaneous successful-replay and current-input failure messages were verified as real stale UI state, not detector inference.
One Playwright role locator did not resolve the native Scene files summary. The control worked through its current accessibility-tree entry; this tooling mismatch is not a product defect.
limitations: This is Assessment B only; no design-health scoring, Assessment A review, parent synthesis, or trend inspection was performed.
No live browser detector overlay because evaluate is read-only and page injection was prohibited.
No source code was edited or implementation fix attempted.
Browser status, screenshots, DOM semantics, and routine reversible UI interactions support the findings; no screen-reader audio session was run.
Source target file paths were enumerated, but manual findings were established from the live interface rather than inferred from implementation.
